_anchors.canvas.w: 48, the same canvas as the target sample. This sample is the declared overshoot, and it changes subject and idiom - it must not also change size, or the failure could be blamed on resolution.
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h / 2, the humanoid's pelvis: the body hangs above it and the legs below
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 4, matched to the target sample so the tone budget is not the variable either
_anchors.frames.walk: 8, matched to the target sample on purpose. What this sample changes is subject and ink weight, nothing else - a Comix Zone frame is a redrawing, and this engine transforms anchored parts, so more frames would only buy a smoother version of the same limitation.
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left, held identical across all four probe samples
_anchors.light.curve: 1.8, matched to the target sample: lighting is never the variable in this probe.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector
_anchors.outline.enabled: on, and heavier than anywhere else: ink is the whole claim of the overshoot
_anchors.outline.inner: on and doing the heaviest work in the probe: ink between parts is the closest this engine comes to a drawn line
_anchors.outline.rim: off. The silhouette edge by value instead of line - a rim on the lit side, an occlusion edge on the shadow side. This is the knob the silhouette round is comparing against outline.enabled, and it is off in every sample that predates the round.
_anchors.body.scale: 1 = identity; the humanoid is authored at 48 px
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.07 turn, from asin(6/16) with a 16 px leg: about 6 px of foot travel, a human stride at this height
_anchors.gait.lift: 2 px = torso height (2 * ry = 16) / 8, the same eighth-of-the-body rule as the arthropod
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0: a drawn-line idiom that also speckles is two idioms
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 75 ms. 8 frames x 75 = the shared 600 ms cycle.
_anchors.playback.scale: 4, because 48 x 4 = 192 px on screen, the shared cell size
_anchors.light.z: the lamp sits slightly on the viewer's side. Backfilled when the depth solver arrived: at -1 every surface faces the light and the body flattens to one tone, at 0 the light grazes and the far half goes black. -0.35 puts the centre of a mass around two thirds up its ramp and still leaves the lit and shadow edges at the two ends.
_anchors.gait.depth: canvas.w / 8 = 6 px. Backfilled with the depth solver; no track in this sample uses the z channel, so it is inert here. It is the body's half-width rather than 0 so that it already means something the day a depth track is added.
